This moment—in which Jane not only reads Rochester's emotional state through his involuntary expression, but also modifies her own behavior based on that reading—exemplifies what literary critic Sandra Gilbert terms "empathetic intelligence," a narrative technique through which Brontë creates psychological intimacy and emotional depth in her character relationships.
